title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A 'disposition pondérée' (E, ≤, |∘|) is a set E with an order ≤ and a symmetric 'disjointness' (incompatibility) relation |∘| that is compatible with the order. Σ_E is the ordered set of 'synthèses' of E. From the surrounding pages, these appear to be the subsets closed under a closure operator W°_E. W°_E behaves like a biorthogonal or regular-open closure: x lies in W°(A) iff every y disjoint from A is disjoint from x. For E'_{≤x} = {x' ∈ E' : x' ≤ x}, write E'_{≤x} |∘| E'_{≤y} to mean that every element of the first set is disjoint from every element of the second.

Corollary 5. Suppose E' ⊂ E is 'dense' in this sense: for all x, y ∈ E, if E'_{≤x} |∘| E'_{≤y} then x |∘| y. Contrapositively: whenever x and y are compatible, some x' ≤ x and y' ≤ y in E' are already compatible. Then there are mutually inverse order-isomorphisms Σ_{E'} ⇄ Σ_E:
- ψ(A') = the W°_E-closure of A' in E;
- φ(A) = A ∩ E'.
In short, the 'completion' of a disposition is unchanged by passing to a dense part. Grothendieck adds that, by Cor. 1, criterion (v), this density condition is a priori stronger than the one in (v).

This is the exact analogue of a standard fact from forcing and Boolean completions. If D is dense in a poset P, then RO(D) ≅ RO(P), with maps 'take the closure' and 'intersect with D'. In orthogonality-space language: a dense sub-orthogonality space has the same lattice of closed subsets.

New section: 'Correspondances entre dispositions et entre synthèses'. Grothendieck begins with the trivial case as an analogy. Let E, E' be bare sets viewed as trivial dispositions (≤ is equality, disjointness is inequality, Σ_E = P(E)). A correspondence R ⊂ E × E' is the same as a map α: E → P(E'), x ↦ R(x). The next page continues:
- α extends to α_*: P(E) → P(E'), the union over the elements of A.
- Such extensions are exactly the arbitrary-sup-preserving maps.
- The transpose β satisfies α_*(A) |∘| A' ⇔ A |∘| β_*(A').
That is, relations correspond to sup-lattice morphisms between power sets, and transposition is adjointness with respect to the disjointness pairing. This is the model he intends to generalise to correspondences between general dispositions and their synthèses.
errors: No clear mathematical error. The proof of Corollary 5 is not given on this page.
Implicit gap: one needs A ∩ E' to be W°_{E'}-closed, and ψ, φ to be mutually inverse and order-preserving. Both follow from the density condition, but this is left unchecked here.
The density condition implicitly forces every non-self-disjoint x to have some element of E' below it (take x = y).

ideas.what: A dense subset E' of a poset with disjointness relation has the same lattice of closed 'synthèses'; the isomorphism is closure one way and intersection with E' the other.
ideas.modern_name: Dense embeddings induce isomorphic Boolean (regular-open) completions; invariance of the closed-subset lattice of an orthogonality space under dense subspaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of forcing / Boolean-valued models (Cohen, Scott, Solovay, Vopěnka, 1960s); orthogonality spaces (Foulis, Dacey, ~1960s–70s)

ideas.what: Relations between sets correspond to sup-preserving maps between power sets; the transposed relation is characterised by a disjointness adjunction α_*(A)|∘|A' ⇔ A|∘|β_*(A').
ideas.modern_name: Rel ≅ category of free complete join-semilattices (Kleisli category of the powerset monad); orthogonality / Galois-type adjunction; Chu-space style duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Birkhoff, Ore Galois connections); sup-lattice formulation Joyal–Tierney 1984

ideas.what: Programme: define 'correspondences' between dispositions and between their synthèses by generalising the trivial-disposition case of relations between sets.
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of orthogonality spaces / ortholattice-valued relations; quantale-enriched relations

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'dispositions pondérées' and their 'synthèses' reproduce, in his own language, the regular-open / Boolean-completion machinery of forcing and orthogonality spaces, including the dense-subset invariance theorem. The record does not seem to note this link between his 1986 'Ateliers' notes and forcing, quantum-logic and orthogonality-space theory. The content itself is standard.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mainly historical interest: it documents Grothendieck independently rebuilding completion theory for 'spaces of parts' in 1986. It would help in placing these unpublished notes; it is not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page states a clean but standard dense-subset invariance result, the analogue of RO(D) ≅ RO(P) in forcing, in Grothendieck's idiosyncratic framework. It then opens a section on correspondences using the well-known Rel ↔ sup-lattice dictionary. It is historically interesting as part of an undocumented 1986 foundational project, but mathematically routine.
transcription_corrections: 'On notera que cor. 1, condition (v), on notera que' — the image reads more like 'On a vu par cor. 1, critère (v), on notera [ou: on sait] que la condition de densité ici est plus forte a priori que celle de (v).'
The formula for ψ(A') has a prefix before W° (looks like '1–' or 's–') that the transcription drops. The subscript under W° is E (corrected over another letter); the reading is uncertain.

The word before 'Analogie' (and before 'Correspondances') is a small superscript, probably 'Ex.' or 'Soit', and was later inserted. In the section title the insertion reads 'dispositions et entre' above the line, giving 'Correspondances entre dispositions et entre synthèses'.
In 'deux ensembles, vus comme dispositions triviales' the struck-out word is 'interp[rétés]', replaced by 'vus comme'.
'(correspondance R)' — the R is written above as an insertion, i.e. 'une "corr" (correspondance R) entre E, E''.
